chunks: 38 - Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Mas'oodi informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar al-Qummi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hassaan al-Razi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: Abdurrahman ibn Abu Najran narrated from al-Qassim, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah regarding the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'Permission (to fight) is given to those upon whom war is made because they are oppressed, and most surely Allah is well able to assist them.'
He said: It concerns al-Qa'im and his companions.

key_terms.أَصْحَابِهِ: his companions, referring to the followers of the Mahdi
key_terms.أُذِنَ: permission was given, referring to the divine permission to fight
key_terms.الْقَائِم: al-Qa'im (The Riser), a title for the Twelfth Imam, Muhammad al-Mahdi
key_terms.يُقَاتَلُونَ: they are fought/they fight, passive participle indicating those who are oppressed and permitted to fight back

ai.seo_question: Who does the verse 'Permission is given to those upon whom war is made' refer to in Shia interpretation?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, the verse is interpreted as a specific prophecy regarding the Twelfth Imam and his followers, linking the general permission to fight (*idhn*) to the unique eschatological context of the Mahdi's rise. This *tafsir* underscores the theological legitimacy of their armed struggle against oppression, framing it not merely as self-defense but as a divinely mandated restoration of justice. The attribution to Imam al-Sadiq via Abu Basir highlights the Imami tradition's view of the Mahdi's campaign as the fulfillment of Quranic promises.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (38) Ali bin al-Husayn al-Mass’oodi narrated from Muhammad bin Yahya al-Attar al-Qummi from Muhammad bin Hassaan ar-Razi from Muhammad bin Ali al-Kufi from Abdurrahman bin Abu Najran from al-Qassim from Abu Baseer that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) had said about the verse, “Permission (to fight) is given to those upon whom war is made because they are oppressed, and most surely Allah is well able to assist them:”
